title: Olive Ascolane
subtitle: Stuffed and fried olives from Ascoli Piceno
excerpt: Olive ascolane are large green olives stuffed with a seasoned meat filling, breaded, and deep-fried until golden. They are the celebrated street food of Ascoli Piceno in Le Marche and appear on every Italian fried food platter. The olives must be large, firm, and pitted in a single spiral cut to hold the filling.
sourceNotes: Olive ascolane all'ascolana is the defining street food and antipasto of Ascoli Piceno in Le Marche. The dish has Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) status in Italy. The classic filling uses mixed meats (veal, pork, chicken) with Parmesan and lemon zest.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Stuff and bread the olives up to 4 hours ahead. Keep in the fridge until ready to fry.

content.text: Olive ascolane require patience in the pitting: each olive is cut in a single spiral cut around the stone, the stone removed, and the flesh wound back around the filling. Large, firm green olives in brine are essential; small or soft olives will break. The filling is a small amount of cooked, seasoned minced meat, just enough to fill the space left by the stone.

items.prepNote: large, firm green olives in brine, stone-in

content.text: Heat a little oil in a frying pan and brown {{pork-mince}} of pork mince and {{beef-mince}} of beef mince together over a medium-high heat, breaking up any lumps. Add {{white-wine-dry}} of white wine and cook until evaporated. Season with {{salt-table}} of salt. Allow to cool completely.

Combine the cooled meat with {{parmesan}} of grated Parmesan, {{lemon}} lemon zest, {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg, and {{eggs}} beaten egg until the mixture comes together. It should be firm enough to shape. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Using a small, sharp knife, cut each of the {{olives-green}} olives in a spiral from top to bottom, following the stone. Remove the stone and the olive should unspool into a single strip. Roll a small amount of filling into the space where the stone was, then wind the olive flesh back around it to reform the olive shape. Squeeze gently to seal.

Set up three shallow bowls: {{plain-flour}} of flour, {{eggs}} of beaten eggs, and {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of breadcrumbs. Roll each stuffed olive in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere. Set aside.
Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of vegetable oil in a deep saucepan to 180C. Fry the olives in batches of 6, turning, for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden. Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot.

items.symptom: The olives fall apart during frying
items.cause: The filling was too wet, or the breading did not adhere properly.
items.fix: Make sure the filling is well-chilled and firm before stuffing. Press the breadcrumbs firmly onto the egg-coated olive. A double breading (egg-breadcrumb-egg-breadcrumb) helps them hold together.

content.text: Olive ascolane are a PGI product of Ascoli Piceno, a walled city in Le Marche. The authentic version uses a local variety called Tenera Ascolana, which is unusually large and meaty with a thin skin that makes spiral pitting easier. Outside Ascoli Piceno, large green Castelvetrano or Sicilian-style olives are a good substitute. The dish appears on nearly every mixed fritto platter in Italian restaurants. In Ascoli Piceno they are sold freshly fried in paper cones from street stalls alongside cremini fritti.
